title: CircuitVAE: Efficient and Scalable Latent Circuit Optimization
problem: Automatically designing fast and space-efficient digital circuits is challenging because circuits are discrete, must implement exact logic, and are expensive to simulate.
motivation: Efficient circuit design is critical for competitive hardware performance and manufacturing costs in modern chip design.
method: CircuitVAE embeds computation graphs into continuous latent space using a variational autoencoder. It learns a neural surrogate model approximating expensive physical simulation and performs gradient-based optimization in the latent space. The approach controls surrogate overfitting and maintains diverse exploration to achieve high sample efficiency and scalability to large circuits.
key_novelty: Using VAE-based latent embeddings with learned simulation surrogates enables efficient gradient-based optimization of discrete circuits.
contributions: CircuitVAE algorithm embedding discrete circuits into continuous latent space for efficient optimization
Learned neural surrogate model of physical simulation for gradient-based search
Superior performance to reinforcement learning and genetic algorithms on large binary adders
Outperforms commercial EDA tools on real-world chip design

metrics.speedup: 64-bit adders faster than RL and genetic algorithm baselines
metrics.area: 64-bit adders smaller than RL and genetic algorithm baselines
metrics.other: Achieves better designs with less than 50% sample budget versus baselines

primary_theme: Learned surrogate optimization for digital circuit design
